questions.topic: Polar addition of HBr to alkene
questions.question: Which step is the rate-determining step in the electrophilic addition of HBr to ethylene?

options.label: A
options.text: Capture of carbocation by bromide anion

options.label: B
options.text: Deprotonation of the alkyl halide product

options.label: C
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the H-Br bond

options.label: D
options.text: Protonation of the alkene double bond to generate the carbocation intermediate

questions.correct_answer: Protonation of the alkene double bond to generate the carbocation intermediate
questions.explanation: Protonation breaks the pi bond and creates a high-energy carbocation, representing the highest activation barrier.

questions.question: What is the geometry and orbital hybridization of a simple alkyl carbocation intermediate?

options.label: A
options.text: Linear with an sp-hybridized carbon

options.label: B
options.text: Tetrahedral with an sp3-hybridized carbon

options.label: C
options.text: Trigonal pyramidal with an sp3 lone pair

options.label: D
options.text: Trigonal planar with an sp2-hybridized carbon and an empty 2p orbital

questions.correct_answer: Trigonal planar with an sp2-hybridized carbon and an empty 2p orbital
questions.explanation: A carbocation has 6 valence electrons in 3 sigma bonds, adopting a planar 120° geometry with an unhybridized vacant p orbital.

questions.question: In an organic mechanism, what does a standard double-barbed curved arrow represent?

options.label: A
options.text: The direction of dipole moment vectors

options.label: B
options.text: The movement of a single unpaired radical electron

options.label: C
options.text: The physical movement of an atomic nucleus

options.label: D
options.text: The movement of a pair of valence electrons from an electron source to an electron sink

questions.correct_answer: The movement of a pair of valence electrons from an electron source to an electron sink
questions.explanation: Curved arrows exclusively track electron pairs flowing from nucleophilic lone pairs/bonds to electrophilic centers.

questions.question: Which characteristic uniquely defines a propagation step in free-radical halogenation?

options.label: A
options.text: Two radicals combine to form a stable sigma bond

options.label: B
options.text: A radical reacts with a non-radical to yield a product and a new radical

options.label: C
options.text: A non-radical homolytically cleaves into two radicals

options.label: D
options.text: A radical is quenched by a transition metal catalyst

questions.correct_answer: A radical reacts with a non-radical to yield a product and a new radical
questions.explanation: Propagation steps maintain the total radical count, sustaining the chain reaction cycle.

questions.question: How does a transition state differ from a reaction intermediate on an energy diagram?

options.label: A
options.text: A transition state has fully formed covalent bonds; an intermediate has none

options.label: B
options.text: A transition state is a local energy maximum; an intermediate is a local energy minimum

options.label: C
options.text: A transition state always has zero activation energy

options.label: D
options.text: A transition state can be isolated in a bottle; an intermediate cannot

questions.correct_answer: A transition state is a local energy maximum; an intermediate is a local energy minimum
questions.explanation: Transition states are fleeting structures at energy peaks (maxima), whereas intermediates occupy energy valleys (minima).

questions.question: According to the Hammond Postulate, what does the transition state of an endothermic step most closely resemble?

options.label: A
options.text: A stable ground-state alkane

options.label: B
options.text: The starting reactant

options.label: C
options.text: The transition state of the reverse reaction

options.label: D
options.text: The high-energy intermediate or product formed in that step

questions.correct_answer: The high-energy intermediate or product formed in that step
questions.explanation: The transition state structure is closest in energy and geometry to the species to which it is closest in free energy.

questions.question: What drives a 1,2-hydride shift in a carbocation intermediate?

options.label: A
options.text: Inductive electron withdrawal by leaving groups

options.label: B
options.text: Repulsion between adjacent positive charges

options.label: C
options.text: Steric clash with solvent molecules

options.label: D
options.text: Thermodynamic relief by converting a less stable carbocation into a more stable carbocation

questions.correct_answer: Thermodynamic relief by converting a less stable carbocation into a more stable carbocation
questions.explanation: Migrating a hydride transfers the positive charge to a more substituted or resonance-stabilized carbon center.

questions.question: What intermediate is formed when propene is protonated by hydronium in aqueous acid?

options.label: A
options.text: Primary propyl carbocation (CH3CH2CH2+)

options.label: B
options.text: Propyl free radical

options.label: C
options.text: Propyl carbanion

options.label: D
options.text: Secondary isopropyl carbocation (CH3-CH(+)-CH3)

questions.correct_answer: Secondary isopropyl carbocation (CH3-CH(+)-CH3)
questions.explanation: Protonation occurs at the terminal carbon to yield the more stable secondary carbocation (Markovnikov rule).

questions.question: Which event represents a termination step in radical bromination?

options.label: A
options.text: Reaction of an alkyl radical with Br2

options.label: B
options.text: Attack of bromine radical on an alkane C-H bond

options.label: C
options.text: Homolysis of Br2 by ultraviolet light

options.label: D
options.text: Combination of two bromine radicals to form Br2

questions.correct_answer: Combination of two bromine radicals to form Br2
questions.explanation: Coupling of two radicals eliminates reactive radical species from the reaction mixture.

questions.question: What is the fundamental role of a nucleophile in a Lewis acid-base reaction?

options.label: B
options.text: Abstracting an electron to become a radical

questions.question: What intermediate is formed when propene is protonated by hydronium in aqueous acid?

options.label: A
options.text: Primary propyl carbocation (CH3CH2CH2+)

options.label: B
options.text: Propyl free radical

options.label: C
options.text: Secondary isopropyl carbocation (CH3-CH(+)-CH3)

options.label: D
options.text: Propyl carbanion

questions.correct_answer: Secondary isopropyl carbocation (CH3-CH(+)-CH3)
questions.explanation: Protonation occurs at the terminal carbon to yield the more stable secondary carbocation (Markovnikov rule).
